During the day, when photosynthesis is active, stomata tend to open to allow CO2 to enter the leaf. This is advantageous because photosynthesis requires CO2, and opening the stomata maximizes the intake of this gas. Additionally, transpiration occurs during the day, which helps in the cooling of the leaf and the transport of water and nutrients from the roots to the rest of the plant. At night, when photosynthesis is not occurring, stomata typically close.
